lead.headline: Anthropic shares fall 9% in second day of trading
lead.summary: Anthropic shares fell 9% on Friday to $88.30, after rising 17% on Thursday in the largest IPO on record, according to The Guardian. The IPO price was $83. The Guardian reports the Nasdaq Composite erased its 2026 gains and the Dow and S&P 500 closed in correction territory. Analysts quoted by The Guardian said investors still doubt that AI spending will pay off.

main.headline: S&P 500 and Dow enter correction as AI stocks sell off
main.summary: The S&P 500 fell 3.59% on Friday to 6,918.45, closing more than 10% below its Oct. 6 record, according to Fortune. The Dow also closed in correction territory, and the Nasdaq Composite gave back its 2026 gains. Chipmakers including Nvidia, AMD and Micron fell roughly 12% to 14%. BBC reports Asian and European markets also fell.

main.headline: Anthropic mathematician claims Claude helped prove Riemann hypothesis
main.summary: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, says he and Claude proved the Riemann hypothesis, including its generalized version. He published a Lean-language version of the proof on his website. The Verge reports the proof has not been independently verified, and Anthropic has not commented. SiliconANGLE reports Alpöge says the full paper runs more than 250,000 pages and has not been released.

main.headline: SEC is probing Nvidia's accounting practices, Reuters reports
main.summary: The US Securities and Exchange Commission is examining Nvidia's accounting practices, according to two people briefed on the matter who spoke to Reuters. The Wall Street Journal had earlier reported a probe but could not determine its focus. The SEC declined to comment, and Reuters could not determine when the inquiry began. Reuters notes that investigations are not evidence of wrongdoing.

main.headline: Jensen Huang to testify publicly before Senate banking panel
main.summary: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will testify publicly before the Senate banking committee, a spokesperson for Chair Tim Scott said. He also agreed to a closed-door House interview on Dec. 1. President Trump said he would like Huang to get a "second chance" as Nvidia CEO. A person familiar with the matter told CNBC the board is not considering his return.
